newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo details plans for restaurants.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo details plans for restaurants.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc said on Tuesday gave more details of its plan to divest its restaurant operations, including selling some chains and taking its New Zealand restaurants public in an initial public offering.

In its first quarter earnings release, PepsiCo chairman and chief executive Roger Enrico said, "We are .. on track with our restaurant strategy. We refranchised 94 stores this quarter and for the full year expect to sell as many or more than we did last year."
He said the company has made "solid progress" readying for a spin-off of its quick service restaurant business including preparing and filing a ruling request with the U.S. Internal Revenue Service.

He said the company completed the sale of both East Side Mario's and Hot 'n Now. It has a pact to sell Chevys and is in active talks to sell both California Pizza Kitchen and PFS, a restaurant distribution company.
"Finally we are targeting the early summer for the initial public offering of our New Zealand restaurants," Enrico said in the release.
